newsitem.title: USA: St. Louis Fed Melzer favors single goal for Fed.
newsitem.headline: St. Louis Fed Melzer favors single goal for Fed.

text.p: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis President Thomas Melzer said on Thursday he favors price stability as the single goal and mandate for the U.S. central bank.

"I am convinced that uncertainty about the Fed's monetary policy goals and methods produces greater volatility in markets than would normally otherwise occur," Melzer told a gathering in Arkadelphia, Arkansas.
The speech was made available in New York.

"An unfocused and uncertain monetary policy causes uncertainty about the nature of price changes in all markets and such confusion interferes with the efficient operation of markets," Melzer also said.
The Fed currently operates under the 1978 Humphrey-Hawkins Act that requires the central bank to seek conditions for both full employment and balanced growth.
"In my view, monetary policy can reliably affect only the price level, so, I favor a mandate that requires the Fed to pursue price stability," Melzer stated.
Turning to the "choice of a specific price level measure for monetary policy," Melzer noted the Consumer Price Index is somewhat distorted by biases.
"Despite its problems, the CPI has a number of advantages that make it a useful index for monetary policy," the St. Louis Fed president added.
Melzer further noted "another source of uncertainty about the course of monetary policy stems from the Fed's fragile political independence."

"I believe that much of the talk abut reducing the Fed's independence stems from frustration over the apparent lack of focus of monetary policy than from concern about the Fed's recent performance," Melzer also said. "The Fed should be held accountable as an institution for what it can, and should, achieve, namely, price stability over time."
